title: Projections comparator file
description: A custom comparator file (`<name>.comparator.yaml`): YAML declarations the rules interpreter runs over the default comparator, sandboxed. Identity passes add correspondences; comparator rules, CEL expressions checked against declared types when the file loads, classify changes, order them into steps and add metadata. See the guide's "Write a custom comparator" and docs/design/declarative-comparators.md.

$schema.description: Editors: `# yaml-language-server: $schema=<url>` at the top of the file works too.

defaults.description: Option values for options the comparison doesn't set. Every expression, functions included, reads them as `options.<name>`; an option the definition sets replaces its default.

functions.description: Named, typed expressions. A body sees its parameters, its own variables and the inputs (`before`, `after`, `lookup`, `options`, `baseline`), never its caller's variables or the file's (share option defaults through `defaults`). The call graph must be acyclic, so every evaluation terminates.

checks.description: Evaluated first, in order. The first `assert` that isn't true fails the comparison with `code` (default `invalid-options`), `path` (default `/options`) and `message`.

identity.description: Identity passes, in order. Each pass sees only the items earlier passes left unmatched. Entity passes all run before relationship passes.

when.description: Skips the pass unless true. Sees `pairs`.

key.description: A key per unmatched `item` (on `side` `before` or `after`): any JSON value, compared as canonical JSON, such as `[item.kind, item.label]`; null skips the item. Items whose key is unique on both sides correspond.

claims.description: The other side's IDs an unmatched `item` claims to be. Each connected group of claims is one change: one-to-one, a split, a merge, or an ambiguous-correspondence error.

classify.description: Evaluated per change, in change order, with `change`, `origin` (the identity pass that matched it, or null), `befores`, `afters`, `beforeItem`, `afterItem`, `changes`, `pairs` and `changeOf`.

summary.description: A string, or null to leave the summary unset.

annotation.description: Any JSON value, or null; available afterwards as `annotations[change.id]`.

steps.description: How the steps are made. Declarative: start from the baseline's steps (dropping changes the comparison no longer has), `add` new steps, `rank` them, then `summary`. Or `value`, one CEL expression for the whole list (the escape hatch).

value.description: The steps, as a list of `{changes, kind?, summary?}`, with `changes`, `annotations`, `pairs` and `changeOf`.

changes.description: Per change (`change`, `origin`, `annotation`): whether it belongs to the new step. Selected changes leave the steps they were in; steps left empty go.

sort.description: Per change: a sort key (null, bool, number, string or list of them; strings in UTF-16 order). Default: entities, then relationships, each by ID.

summary.description: With `members`, the step's changes: a string, or null for none.

place.description: Where the step goes: `start`, `end` (default), `before:<kind>` (before the first step of that kind, else last) or `after:<kind>` (after the last, else first).

rank.description: Per change (`change`, `origin`, `annotation`): a number, a list of numbers (the least counts) or null. Steps are stably sorted by their best-ranked change; steps without a rank keep their order after the ranked ones.

summary.description: Per step, with `step`, `members` and `lead` (the first change with the best rank, or null): a string, or null to keep the step's summary.

metadata.description: Comparison metadata keys, merged over the baseline's; a null value is omitted.

variables.description: Named values, evaluated once and in order, each able to use the earlier ones; expressions read them as `variables.<name>`.

values.description: The values a variable or parameter can take. A `match` on it warns about keys outside them and values it doesn't handle.

type.description: A declared type: `string`, `int`, `double`, `bool`, `dyn`, `list<T>`, `map<K, V>`, `optional<T>`, or one of the protocol's object types (`Extraction`, `Entity`, `Relationship`, `Item`, `Change`, `Step`, `Comparison`, `Side`, `Lookup`, `Finding`, `Classification`, `Pairs`).
